# 1 Enoch Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of the Watchers

---

**1** These are the words of Enoch's blessing — the blessing he spoke over the chosen and the righteous, who will be alive on the day of anguish, when every wicked and godless person is swept away.

**2** He lifted up his voice and said: I, Enoch — a righteous man whose eyes God opened — I saw a vision of the Holy One, a vision of heaven itself. The angels revealed it to me; from them I heard everything, and from them I came to understand what I saw. But it was not meant for my own generation — it was meant for a generation far in the future.

**3** About the chosen I spoke, and I declared: The Holy and Great One will come out from where he dwells,

**4** and the eternal God will set foot on the earth — on Mount Sinai — and appear from his heavenly camp in the full force of his power.

**5** Everyone will be terrified. The Watchers will shake, and uncontrollable fear will grip them to the very edges of the world.

**6** The towering mountains will tremble, the high hills will collapse, melting like wax in a furnace.

**7** The earth will crack wide open. Everything on it will be destroyed, and judgment will fall on all people.

**8** But with the righteous, God will make peace. He will shield his chosen ones and show them mercy. They will all belong to God; they will flourish, and every one of them will be blessed. He will come to their aid, and light will dawn upon them, and he will give them peace.

**9** Look! He is coming with countless thousands of his holy ones to carry out judgment on everyone — to wipe out the ungodly and convict every living person of every ungodly act they have committed and every brutal word that godless sinners have hurled against him.


---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering aimed at modern English readability. Ge'ez idioms are rendered by their functional English equivalents. Theological terms are translated for impact rather than etymological precision.*
